knowledge.productBrief:
# Product brief

## Product
A native, cosy Mac workplace where an owner hires named AI employees,
gives them outcomes, and receives inspectable local work.

## Audience
A solo founder or very small company that wants useful non-technical
employees without configuring prompts or workflow infrastructure.

## Current proof
An executive assistant, a researcher, a content team, explicit skills,
read-only research permission, local persistence, and bounded handoffs.

## Constraints
Start with non-technical work, no external writes, no cloud credentials,
and no claim of autonomy that the current product cannot demonstrate.

researchAssignments.context: Compare at least three roles. Prefer current primary product documentation and credible first-party evidence. Exclude software engineering. End with one narrow employee definition and the first weekly duty it should own.
researchAssignments.outcome: Recommend the single best non-technical AI employee for a solo founder to use every week after the research employee, based on repeatability, measurable output, permission risk, and suitability for this local Mac-first product.

skillDefinitions.instructions: Summarize only persisted goals, tasks, blockers, permissions, and artifacts. Separate completed work from pending work and end with the next owner decision.
skillDefinitions.name: Executive briefing
skillDefinitions.purpose: Keep the owner oriented around current work and decisions.
skillDefinitions.successCriteria: The brief is attributable, contains no invented progress, and names one clear next action.

skillDefinitions.instructions: Break the outcome into the existing bounded tasks, keep ownership explicit, review handoffs, and stop at the configured revision limit.
skillDefinitions.name: Outcome ownership
skillDefinitions.purpose: Own a bounded organizational outcome and coordinate specialists toward it.
skillDefinitions.successCriteria: The outcome ends with approved work or a precise owner blocker, never an infinite review loop.

skillDefinitions.instructions: Ground the question in the product brief. Use external sources only when web research is granted, cite URLs when used, and distinguish evidence from owner claims.
skillDefinitions.name: Audience research
skillDefinitions.purpose: Find the useful audience question that the content should answer.
skillDefinitions.successCriteria: Research identifies a concrete reader question, evidence basis, and article direction without fabricated sources.

skillDefinitions.instructions: Write from the product brief and research artifact, preserve claim boundaries, and make the result independently readable rather than summarizing the transcript.
skillDefinitions.name: Evidence-based writing
skillDefinitions.purpose: Turn approved evidence and direction into a useful article.
skillDefinitions.successCriteria: The draft answers the audience question, traces its evidence, and is ready for editorial review.

skillDefinitions.instructions: Return a clear approve or revise verdict with focused evidence. Do not request more than the bounded revision limit permits.
skillDefinitions.name: Editorial review
skillDefinitions.purpose: Evaluate content against its outcome, evidence, and safe claims.
skillDefinitions.successCriteria: The verdict is actionable, grounded in the artifact, and either approves the work or identifies one bounded correction.

skillDefinitions.instructions: Summarize completed tasks, created artifacts, unresolved blockers, capability use, and the recommended next action.
skillDefinitions.name: Owner reporting
skillDefinitions.purpose: Leave the owner a concise account of completed work and next decisions.
skillDefinitions.successCriteria: The report matches persisted state and lets the owner resume without reading the full activity timeline.
